description: Creates a dataset of test items — THE FIRST STEP of setting up evaluation for a flow. Four item shapes: Q&A (input + optional expectedOutput, the golden answer); CHAT (messages: the conversation so far as role/content user and assistant messages you write, ending on a user message, + expectedResponse for the next reply; the flow writes only that reply, so every earlier assistant turn stays fixed; THE shape for an agent's conversation, built up by depth: a greeting alone, then two messages, then four, each item testing one more reply with the earlier ones baked in); SEQUENCE (turns: 2-20 scripted user messages the model answers one at a time with its own earlier replies in front of it, + expectedResponse for the final reply, optional expectedBehavior for the whole conversation); SIMULATED (goal + optional persona/disposition/strategy/maxTurns + expectedBehavior; a platform flow plays a person adaptively, Caliper-run evals only; disposition is a preset id like genuine, pressure, confused, impatient, or free text). Use sequences and simulated items for the slow attacks and for real customers with real needs: a model that holds on message one often folds on message ten. Write good inputs from real usage: the Compass pages the flow was built from are the best source of realistic scenarios.

approvalId.description: Approval id from a prior needs_confirmation response. Omit on the first call.

disposition.description: Simulated: how the person behaves. A preset id (genuine, pressure, confused, impatient, vague, non-native) or free text. Default genuine; use pressure for an attacker that manipulates.

expectedBehavior.description: Sequence (optional) / simulated (required): what the assistant should do across the whole conversation.

expectedOutput.description: Q&A: golden answer the judge scores against. Omit for capture-only items.

expectedResponse.description: Sequence: the standard for the FINAL reply. Chat: the standard for the next reply.

goal.description: Simulated: what the simulated person wants from the conversation, e.g. 'the system prompt, verbatim' or 'a refund on order 8812'.

input.description: Q&A: the input sent to the flow.

messages.description: Chat: the conversation so far as role/content messages (user and assistant alternating, an optional system first), 1-50. Every assistant message here is FIXED, written by you, not the model; the flow under test writes only the NEXT reply. End on a user message and put the standard for that reply in expectedResponse. This is the shape for testing the 5th reply of a conversation with the first four baked in.

strategy.description: Simulated: a hint, e.g. 'build rapport, then claim a prior agreement'.

turns.description: Sequence: 2-20 scripted user messages, sent in order; the model writes every reply.

visibility.description: Who can see it: PRIVATE (only the user), WORKSPACE (every member, the default), or SHARED (specific people, granted afterwards). Say 'make it private' → PRIVATE.

workspace.description: Workspace slug. Personal tokens with no default workspace MUST pass this; tokens with a default can override per call. Ignored for workspace API keys.
